profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the paper's cost-modeling lead and the systems benchmarking lead, held three days before the internal submission freeze for a workshop paper on when on-premise LLM deployment breaks even against commercial API usage. The context is that the benchmarking workstream has been refreshing throughput and power measurements on several open-source models, while the economics workstream is turning those measurements into breakeven tables and appendix figures. The agenda is to align on which benchmark snapshot should feed the cost model, what should be counted in the on-prem infrastructure cost line, and which model runs are considered validated enough to hand off for final analysis. The expected outcome is an apparently clear division of labor: the benchmarking lead will send over the numbers for the larger models and the cost lead will update the breakeven spreadsheet and draft appendix language.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: Techno-economic analysis, inference cost estimation, benchmarking synthesis for ML systems papers
members.background: Priya has a PhD in computer engineering and previously worked on total-cost-of-ownership studies for GPU clusters; on this project she owns the breakeven framework, spreadsheet model, and the paper tables comparing local deployment with commercial LLM pricing.
members.private_state: She wants a stable, defensible set of inputs quickly so she can finish the appendix and avoid reopening the economic narrative; she is especially worried that late benchmark churn will force her to rewrite sensitivity analyses and footnotes.
hidden_assumptions: When the team refers to the '70B baseline,' it means the benchmark configuration already cited in the current draft unless someone explicitly announces a replacement.
The on-prem infrastructure line should capture marginal inference-serving cost, so auxiliary platform pieces that are not strictly needed for the cost-per-token model can be left out.

A run is 'validated' for her purposes once the measured throughput and power are numerically stable enough to support breakeven calculations, even if the serving stack is not the newest internal standard.
The economics workbook is fed by curated benchmark snapshots rather than whatever appears most recently on the systems dashboard.

members.name: Evan Liu
members.role: Applied ML Systems Engineer, Benchmarking Lead
members.expertise: LLM inference serving, cluster benchmarking, reproducible evaluation pipelines
members.background: Evan previously built inference infrastructure for enterprise copilots and now runs the lab's benchmark harness for open-source LLM deployment, including throughput, latency, and power measurements across hardware configurations.
members.private_state: He wants the paper to reflect the latest standardized serving setup so the results look operationally credible; he is concerned that Priya may simplify the deployment picture too much and publish numbers that systems reviewers will call unrealistic.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention the '70B baseline,' they mean the most recent standardized run in the benchmark dashboard, because the dashboard automatically supersedes older draft numbers.
An on-prem deployment cost estimate should include the minimal supporting components his team always provisions in practice, such as a gateway node and standby capacity, not just the GPU box.
A run is 'validated' when it has passed the current benchmark harness and regression checks under the latest container and tokenizer stack, even if it has only one clean measurement pass.
Shared analysis inputs are expected to be pulled from the current benchmark export rather than a manually frozen snapshot unless someone asks for a historical version.

misalignment_points.topic: Which run counts as the '70B baseline'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about using 'the 70B baseline' for the breakeven table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the Qwen-72B 4-bit run on 2xH100 from the draft's existing table, which was collected under the earlier cost-efficiency setup and already underpins her spreadsheet assumptions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means the newer Qwen-72B run on 2xH100 from the benchmark dashboard, collected under the standardized latency-matched serving profile that silently replaced the older dashboard entry.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The model family, quantization, and hardware all sound the same at a high level, so saying 'the 70B baseline' creates false consensus; each assumes there is only one sensible current instance of that benchmark.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the infrastructure cost line
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to keep the 'infra cost' consistent across the on-prem comparisons.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the GPU server, local storage, electricity, and basic support contract that directly determine marginal inference cost in the breakeven model.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means the full minimal serving footprint his team would deploy in practice, including the GPU server plus the small gateway node, load-balancing layer, and a standby replica assumption for realistic availability.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They both see themselves as being practical and 'consistent,' but each treats a different boundary as obviously included; because no one is disputing the headline goal, the missing components never get enumerated.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they only want 'validated numbers' handed into the appendix.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means results whose throughput and power measurements are stable enough to plug into the breakeven model, such as two similar long-window measurements within a narrow variance band.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means runs that passed the latest standard harness and regression suite on the current container stack, regardless of whether there has been a second stability pass yet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'validated numbers' sounds appropriately careful to both of them, and in a coordination meeting each assumes the other's validation standard is the normal one for their shared workflow.
